area: renderer boot to first interactive frame (index.html -> index chunk -> boot chunk -> App -> WorkspaceRoot -> viewer -> explorer usable -> Cmd+P usable)
timeline:
Measured live over CDP against the installed build (~/Applications/Horus.app, app.asar built 12:32:28 from the current tree). Two real sessions probed, ports 9490 and 9491.

t=0 navigation start (src/renderer/index.html, file:// inside app.asar). responseEnd 45.5 ms, domInteractive 89.1 ms, DOMContentLoaded 93.3 ms, load 95.9 ms.
t=46-90 ms  index.html head: CSP meta (electron.vite.config.ts:17-45), 5-rule inline critical style (index.html:8-16), <script type=module src=./assets/index-CaNbrFQL.js> + <link rel=preload as=style boot-B2Joa_jX.css> + <link rel=modulepreload boot-B2rRKoKF.js> injected by preloadBootChunkPlugin (electron.vite.config.ts:136-163). Only <div class="boot-drag"> (index.html:20) is on screen.
t=87.6-92.8 ms  horus:renderer-loaded (main.tsx:4 -> startupMetrics.ts:13). main.tsx is 9 lines: stamp restore hint on <html>, fire getSessionSnapshot(), dynamic import('./boot').
t=100-112 ms  first-paint (dark ground, no content).
t=93-142 ms  index-CaNbrFQL.js __vitePreload creates <link rel=stylesheet boot-B2Joa_jX.css> (171,776 B, 1,266 rules) and AWAITS its load before importing boot-B2rRKoKF.js (439,332 B). boot.tsx:14-15 fires the two fontsource CSS imports (not awaited); boot.tsx:17 loadPreferences() reads localStorage; boot.tsx:18 initialWorkspacePaint(window.repository.cachedWorkspace) - already parsed in preload via ipcRenderer.sendSync (src/preload/index.ts:55).
t=142-233 ms  ONE 91 ms long task (PerformanceObserver longtask buffered:true -> {name:"self", start:142, duration:91}). This is boot.tsx:20-30 await Promise.all([preloadWorkspaceRoot(), preloadWorkspaceViewer(...)]) resolving and every module body executing back to back - WorkspaceRoot 268,669 B, copyFilePath 301,887 B, ViewerProviders 10,796 B, useReviewLoadState 12,513 B, pierre-dark 30,549 B, BackToTopButton 611,171 B, MultiFileReview 103,345 B - then createRoot().render() (boot.tsx:32-38) and React's first render+commit.
t=162.8-171.4 ms  horus:explorer-committed (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1297) and horus:viewer-committed (MultiFileReview.tsx:1065 / DiffSurface.tsx:535) - child layout effects.
t=177.9-197.2 ms  horus:react-committed (App.tsx:636) - parent layout effect runs last.
t=284 ms  first-contentful-paint. The window is blank from 112 ms to 284 ms.
t=4541.7 ms (port-9490 session)  horus:snapshot-ready (App.tsx:698) - main finally delivers the restored snapshot; this is the lead's confirmed 3.8 s git ls-files --others --ignored. In the port-9491 session the mark never fired within 100 s because applySnapshot returns early on snapshotLooksUnchanged (App.tsx:696-697) before marking.

Steady state: 218 light-DOM nodes, 1,291 including shadow roots, 26 rendered tree rows (@pierre/trees virtualizes - nothing renders 20k rows), 14-16 MB JS heap, 4 stylesheets, 14 font faces all font-display:swap with only the two latin subsets loaded, full style recalc 0.2 ms.

Cmd+P: the palette chunk is 10,060 B and is warmed twice - requestIdleCallback once a snapshot exists (App.tsx:977-982) and on the first Meta keydown (App.tsx:219). Opening is instant. The cost is typing: useRepositorySearch lives inside AppLayout (App.tsx:552) and workspaceContentSearch (App.tsx:555-558) is rebuilt per keystroke in single-file view, breaking the memo on AgentSessionLayout and re-rendering WorkspaceRoot -> RepositoryWorkspace -> Explorer on every character.

findings.title: boot.tsx awaits the whole viewer chunk graph (~1.87 MB) before createRoot().render() - regression introduced by e18053e
findings.mechanism: When a cached workspace exists (the normal restore path, and the path Raycast horus:// also lands on) mountApp blocks on Promise.all([preloadWorkspaceRoot(), preloadWorkspaceViewer(cachedPaint.workspaceView)]) before React mounts anything. That resolves only after WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js (268,669 B) + its static deps copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js (301,887 B), ViewerProviders (10,796 B), useReviewLoadState (12,513 B), pierre-dark (30,549 B) + the viewer branch BackToTopButton-C2hfwQQH.js (611,171 B) + MultiFileReview-B7hs9zS1.js (103,345 B) have all been read from the asar, parsed and executed. Nothing is on screen but the 40px drag strip for that whole time. React already has both fallbacks for this: App.tsx:340-357 CachedWorkspaceFallback renders the cached sidebar when getLoadedWorkspaceRoot() is null, and WorkspaceSkeleton.tsx:41-52 WorkspaceCodeSkeleton covers the viewer slot.
findings.evidence: git show e18053e -- src/renderer/src/boot.tsx shows the file was created in that commit with the blocking await; the code it replaced in main.tsx was fire-and-forget: "void preloadWorkspaceRoot().catch(...)" with the comment "but do not await them". Live marks: horus:renderer-loaded 92.8 ms, single longtask start 142 dur 91, horus:react-committed 197.2 ms, first-contentful-paint 284 ms, first-paint 112 ms. Chunk import graph from the built output: WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js statically imports copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js, ViewerProviders-CwKApq7y.js, useReviewLoadState-nxeBxob_.js, pierre-dark-CyvmCCZW.js; MultiFileReview-B7hs9zS1.js statically imports BackToTopButton-C2hfwQQH.js.
findings.fix: Delete the await. Replace boot.tsx:20-30 with unconditional fire-and-forget preloads: `void preloadWorkspaceRoot().catch(() => undefined)` and, when cachedPaint.snapshot != null, `void preloadWorkspaceViewer(cachedPaint.workspaceView).catch(() => undefined)`; keep the existing sessionSnapshot.then branch for the no-cache case. Move createRoot().render() to run immediately after loadPreferences(). App already renders CachedWorkspaceFallback (App.tsx:487-493) while WorkspaceRoot is null and re-renders through useSyncExternalStore(subscribeWorkspaceRoot) (App.tsx:665-669) the moment the chunk lands, so no code change is needed downstream. If the fallback flash is the reason the await was added, gate it on a 60 ms timer instead of on chunk load.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 90-140 ms warm to first contentful frame; substantially more on the first launch after an update when the V8 code cache is cold (2.6 MB of chunks measured at 37 ms of pure V8 parse plus full top-level execution)

findings.title: BackToTopButton-C2hfwQQH.js is a 611 KB shared viewer chunk: 257 KB @pierre/diffs + 146 KB parse5 + ~90 KB micromark/mdast/hast, all on the pre-mount path
findings.mechanism: Rollup put every module shared by DiffSurface and MultiFileReview into one chunk and named it after the smallest module in it (BackToTopButton.tsx, 699 bytes) - that is why the name says nothing about the 611 KB inside. Byte attribution decoded from BackToTopButton-C2hfwQQH.js.map: @pierre/diffs 256,834 (FileDiff 41,023, style.js 37,856, InteractionManager 31,320, DiffHunksRenderer 26,076, VirtualizedFileDiff 25,549, File 23,120, VirtualizedFile 12,836, FileRenderer 11,260), parse5 146,415 (parser/index 46,732, tokenizer/index 45,835), micromark-core-commonmark 27,520, mdast-util-to-markdown 11,692, mdast-util-to-hast 10,895, mdast-util-from-markdown 10,371, micromark 9,555, hast-util-to-jsx-runtime 5,943, hast-util-raw 5,622, hast-util-sanitize 5,134, unified 4,160, plus entities 15,495. parse5 is there only because rehype-raw needs a real HTML parser; the whole markdown pipeline is dragged in statically by ReviewComments/GitHubMarkdownContent, which the viewers import eagerly even though a review usually has zero comments.
findings.fix: In src/renderer/src/ReviewComments.tsx replace the static import of GitHubMarkdownContent with `const GitHubMarkdownContent = lazy(() => import("./GitHubMarkdownContent"))` and wrap its uses in {body}}>. That moves react-markdown + rehype-raw + rehype-sanitize + remark-gfm + parse5 + micromark + the mdast/hast stack (~240 KB) out of the shared viewer chunk into a chunk fetched only when a comment thread is actually rendered. Verify afterwards that the shared chunk drops to ~370 KB and that parse5 no longer appears in its source map.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 25-45 ms warm (parse + top-level execution of ~240 KB), and it removes 240 KB from every cold start

findings.title: The whole shiki/textmate/oniguruma tokenizer stack (302 KB chunk) is loaded and executed on the MAIN thread at startup, duplicating the highlighter worker
findings.file: out/renderer/assets/copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js (pulled in statically by WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js and ViewerProviders-CwKApq7y.js)
findings.mechanism: Byte attribution of copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js.map: @shikijs/vscode-textmate 42,538, shiki langs-bundle-full 28,709, oniguruma-to-es 26,658, oniguruma-parser 23,987, @shikijs/core 18,141, property-information 17,936, @shikijs/primitive 13,524, @shikijs/engine-oniguruma 7,005, hast-util-to-html 7,989, @pierre/diffs WorkerPoolManager 20,340 + parsePatchFiles 9,541 + iterateOverDiff 9,382. Highlighting itself runs in worker-JZSb44JN.js (207,560 B), which loads its own copy - so ~140 KB of tokenizer machinery is parsed and its module bodies run on the main thread during the 91 ms boot long task for nothing. The build already proves this class of trim is possible: dropShikiWasmPlugin (electron.vite.config.ts:165-181) stubs shiki/wasm out and saved a 622 KB inlined wasm chunk, and trimShikiThemesPlugin (electron.vite.config.ts:66-134) rewrites shiki/dist/themes.mjs.
findings.fix: Add a renderer-only plugin next to dropShikiWasmPlugin that resolves @shikijs/engine-oniguruma, oniguruma-to-es and shiki/dist/langs-bundle-full to throwing stubs, registered in the `renderer.plugins` array but NOT in `renderer.worker.plugins` (electron.vite.config.ts:231-234 already keeps a separate plugin list for the worker, so the worker keeps the real modules). Then check that the main-thread path never calls createHighlighter - grep the copyFilePath chunk for createOnigurumaEngine/createHighlighterCore, which currently matches 3 times. If @pierre/diffs genuinely needs the shiki types on the main thread, switch those to `import type`.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 20-40 ms warm; ~140 KB off the pre-mount path

findings.title: @pierre/trees path-store (62 KB) and 30 @pierre/icons (23 KB) sit in the 439 KB boot chunk only because treeExpansion.ts calls prepareFileTreeInput
findings.mechanism: boot-B2rRKoKF.js byte attribution: react-dom 180,847, app code 159,571, @pierre/trees 62,315, @pierre/icons 23,207, react 8,542, scheduler 3,680. The @pierre/trees sources in the boot map are the entire SoA path-store: path-store/src/{builder,store,canonical,projection,events,cleanup,soa-node-store,flatten,sort,segments,path,state,child-index,options,internal-types}.js plus preparedInput.js. Nothing in the boot chunk renders a tree - the real FileTree lives in WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js, which already carries 175,231 bytes of @pierre/trees. The only entry-chunk consumer is workspaceMode.ts:47/48 firstOpenPathForSnapshot -> treeExpansion.ts:21 orderPathsForTree -> prepareFileTreeInput, reached from boot.tsx (via workspaceMode) and App.tsx:642. Measured cost of that call: 4.07 ms at the user's real 2,621 paths, 34.87 ms at 20,000 paths.
findings.fix: Replace firstTreePath with a local folders-first comparator in treeExpansion.ts that does not import @pierre/trees - the only property it needs is "directories before files at each level, byte order within a level", which is a ~15-line sort on split paths, or simply the first path whose parent directory is the alphabetically-first top-level directory. Keep orderPathsForTree (used by RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:381 inside the WorkspaceRoot chunk) importing @pierre/trees. Then verify the boot chunk no longer lists path-store sources. Separately, audit the 30 @pierre/icons in boot: AppView.tsx:2-24 imports 23 icons for the Titlebar and Welcome; the ones only used by Welcome (IconFolder, IconClockArrow, IconCodeFolder...) can move into a lazily imported Welcome.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 10-20 ms warm (parse+execute of 85 KB), plus removes a 35 ms tail risk at 20k paths (see RB-05)

findings.title: App re-runs initialWorkspacePaint() and firstOpenPathForSnapshot() on every render, and React Compiler compiled zero of App
findings.mechanism: Both are plain call expressions in the component body, not lazy useState initializers, so they run on every render of the root component. initialWorkspacePaint (shared/workspaceCache.ts:110-121) calls parseSelectedPath -> paths.includes(raw), a linear scan of up to MAX_CACHED_PATHS = 20,000. firstOpenPathForSnapshot (workspaceMode.ts:43-49) falls through to firstTreePath(snapshot.paths) -> prepareFileTreeInput over every path whenever the repo is clean or is a plain folder - 34.87 ms at 20,000 paths, measured. Confirmed unmemoized in the shipped build: decoding boot-B2rRKoKF.js.map at App.tsx:639 gives the generated text `const a=om(window.repository?.cachedWorkspace??null),[o,c]=C.useState(a.snapshot),[d,f]=C.useState(a.selectedPath??(a.snapshot==null?null:na(a.snapshot)))` - no memo-cache guard. Worse, React Compiler bailed on App entirely: scanning 30,000 generated characters from the start of App (minified name Q3) finds zero `qe.c(N)` memo-cache calls, while the same chunk contains 34 of them for other components (WorkspaceRoot chunk 27, MultiFileReview chunk 17). So none of App's ~40 hooks and derived values are compiler-memoized.
findings.evidence: Generated source at App.tsx:639 quoted above, extracted by decoding the VLQ mappings of boot-B2rRKoKF.js.map. Memo-cache call counts: `grep -oE "[A-Za-z$_]{1,3}\.c\([0-9]+\)" boot-B2rRKoKF.js | wc -l` = 34 overall, 0 within App's span. Bench (bun/JSC, V8 comparable): prepareFileTreeInput 4.07 ms @2,621 real paths / 34.87 ms @20,000; paths.includes(last) 0.06 ms @20,000.
findings.fix: App.tsx:639 -> `const [cachedPaint] = useState(() => initialWorkspacePaint(window.repository?.cachedWorkspace ?? null))`. App.tsx:641-642 -> `useState(() => cachedPaint.selectedPath ?? (cachedPaint.snapshot == null ? null : firstOpenPathForSnapshot(cachedPaint.snapshot)))`. Separately, find the compiler bailout: run the build with babel-plugin-react-compiler `{ target: "19", logger: { logEvent: (f, e) => e.kind === "CompileError" && console.error(f, e) } }` (electron.vite.config.ts:216-220) and fix whatever App does that the compiler rejects - the likely candidates are the useEffectEvent uses (App.tsx:214, 758, 830, 894) or the mutable folderPickerOpenRef writes inside callbacks. Getting App compiled is worth more than any single micro-fix here.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0-35 ms per App render depending on repo size; on a 20k-path folder this is 35 ms of jank on every root state change

findings.title: Typing in Cmd+P re-renders the entire workspace once per keystroke while the single-file view is active
findings.mechanism: useRepositorySearch owns the query state and lives inside AppLayout, so every keystroke re-renders AppLayout. App.tsx:555-558 then builds `{ query: search.query, results: search.contentResults }` - a fresh object identity per keystroke whenever workspaceView === "file" - and passes it to AgentSessionLayout, which is memo()'d (App.tsx:355). That one prop breaks the memo, so AgentSessionLayout -> WorkspaceRoot -> RepositoryWorkspace -> Explorer/DiffSurface all re-render on every character. It is compounded by useRepositorySearch.ts:64-96: the effect has `query` in its deps and unconditionally calls setContentResults([]) (a brand-new array every time) plus setSearchingContent(true) plus an IPC window.repository.cancelContentSearch(), outside any transition - so each keystroke costs two extra synchronous renders of that whole subtree on top of the one the input caused. The palette itself is careful (CommandPalette.tsx:340-346 wraps onQueryChange in startTransition; useRepositorySearch.ts:36 uses useDeferredValue) and that care is undone by the effect writing state synchronously afterwards. In multi-file review the memo does hold, because workspaceContentSearch is undefined - which matches the user reporting the jank as intermittent.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:555-558 useMemo deps are [search.contentResults, search.query, workspace.workspaceView]; search.contentResults gets a new [] identity from useRepositorySearch.ts:69 and :77 on every keystroke. contentSearch is threaded down RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1290 -> :1527 -> :946 to DiffSurface.tsx:368-371. Bench: rankFilePaths over the fuzzy index costs 0.38 ms at the user's 2,621 paths and 1.3-3.1 ms at 20,000 - so the ranking is NOT the jank, the re-render is.
findings.fix: (1) useRepositorySearch.ts:69 and :77 - make the clears identity-stable: `setContentResults((current) => current.length === 0 ? current : EMPTY_RESULTS)` with a module-level frozen EMPTY_RESULTS, and only call setSearchingContent(true) when it is currently false. (2) App.tsx:555-558 - key the memo on a deferred query (`const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(search.query)`) so the workspace sees at most one update per idle slice. (3) Better still, stop passing content-search state through the workspace tree at all: expose it via a small context that only DiffSurface (DiffSurface.tsx:368) subscribes to, so a keystroke can never re-render Explorer or the tree. (4) Wrap the effect body's state writes in startTransition.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 5-30 ms of main-thread work removed per keystroke, which is the difference between a dropped frame and none

findings.title: 172 KB / 1,266-rule stylesheet is strictly serial in front of the app JS, and most of it styles lazily loaded surfaces
findings.line: whole file (202,110 bytes source, 171,776 bytes built as boot-B2Joa_jX.css)
findings.mechanism: boot.tsx:11 imports styles.css into the boot chunk, so Vite emits it as boot-B2Joa_jX.css; the entry shim index-CaNbrFQL.js creates the <link rel=stylesheet> and awaits its load event before it even starts importing boot-B2rRKoKF.js (that is what the __vitePreload wrapper does for .css deps). The rel=preload injected by preloadBootChunkPlugin keeps it warm but does not remove the serialization. Class-prefix census of the file: agent 244 selectors, review 190, performance 155, pr 150, settings 61, markdown 58, git 53, world 50, command 45, welcome 44, terminal 41 - every one of those belongs to a component that is lazy() or dynamically imported (TerminalDock, GitHubPanel, SettingsPage, AgentPanel, CommandPalette, PerformanceChart). Live probe shows a full style recalculation over the mounted tree is only 0.2 ms, so this is purely load/parse/serialize cost, not selector-matching cost.
findings.fix: Split styles.css: keep only the tokens (:root, the 163 custom properties), reset, app-shell, titlebar, workspace/sidebar and explorer rules in the boot stylesheet, and move the agent, performance, pr, settings, terminal, markdown, welcome and command-palette blocks into per-component CSS imported from the lazy components themselves (`import "./AgentPanel.css"` inside AgentPanel.tsx) so Vite emits them as sibling chunk CSS. WorkspaceSkeleton.tsx:44 already demonstrates the alternative pattern (<style href precedence>) if separate files are unwanted. Target: boot CSS under 60 KB.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 10-25 ms to first paint (the stylesheet load is serial in front of the boot chunk import)

findings.title: PerformanceHud is mounted unconditionally and fires a main-process IPC metrics sample the instant it mounts, during the startup window
findings.line: 118 (void sample() at mount), 22-23 (2s open / 15s collapsed polling), AppView.tsx:36 and :234 (mounted whenever snapshot != null)
findings.mechanism: The HUD is a static import in AppView (AppView.tsx:36) so it is 8,084 bytes inside the 439 KB boot chunk, and Titlebar renders it eagerly (AppView.tsx:231-235). Its mount effect calls `void sample()` immediately (PerformanceHud.tsx:118), which invokes repository.getPerformanceMetrics over IPC; in main that is Electron app.getAppMetrics(), executed on the same main-process thread that the lead measured spending 3.8 s in `git ls-files --others --ignored` during restore. It then polls forever at 15 s collapsed / 2 s open, and re-samples on every visibilitychange.
findings.fix: Make it `const PerformanceHud = lazy(() => import("./PerformanceHud"))` in AppView.tsx and wrap it in <Suspense fallback={null}> so the 8 KB and the @pierre/icons IconCiWarningFill leave the boot chunk. Replace PerformanceHud.tsx:118 `void sample()` with `const idle = window.requestIdleCallback(() => void sample()); ...cancelIdleCallback(idle)`, and do not sample at all until popoverOpen has been true once - render an em dash until then, which is what it already shows when metrics == null (PerformanceHud.tsx:172).
findings.estimatedGainMs: 3-8 ms of renderer work, plus removes one IPC round trip and one app.getAppMetrics() call from the main process during the startup git walk

findings.title: The startup benchmark probes a selector that a file-view restore can never satisfy, which is why it fails rather than reporting a slow number
findings.mechanism: All three selectors still exist in the source: #repository-explorer at Explorer.tsx:120, .multi-file-review at MultiFileReview.tsx:882, .multi-file-code-view at retainedWorldCodeView.tsx:215. But .multi-file-code-view only ever renders INSIDE .multi-file-review, so the two-selector list is really one selector, and it only mounts when workspaceView === "multi". The user's ~/Library/Application Support/Horus/last-workspace.json currently stores workspaceView:"file" (3,026 paths, 12 statuses, root materialsx-core-3), so initialWorkspacePaint (workspaceCache.ts:110-121) starts App in file view - and App.applyStartupSnapshot only calls changeWorkspaceView(automaticWorkspaceView(...)) when `appliedSnapshotRef.current?.root !== restoredSnapshot.root` (App.tsx:907-909), which is false because the cached paint already set that ref to the same root. So the review surface never mounts and the benchmark throws "The restored explorer and review surface did not become usable" no matter how fast startup is. I observed exactly this live: one session reported review:false after 24 s of uptime; a later session whose cache held "multi" reported review:true.
findings.evidence: CDP probe of the running app returned {explorer:true, review:false, diffPanel:true, treeRows:26} on the port-9490 session and {explorer:true, review:true} on the port-9491 session. last-workspace.json parsed: workspaceView "file", 3,026 paths, 12 statuses.
findings.fix: Stop probing DOM classes - the app already records exactly the milestones the benchmark wants. Replace scripts/benchmark-startup.mjs:102-108 with a probe that reads `performance.getEntriesByName("horus:explorer-committed")[0]?.startTime` and `performance.getEntriesByName("horus:viewer-committed")[0]?.startTime` (marked at RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1297, MultiFileReview.tsx:1065 and DiffSurface.tsx:535, so the viewer mark fires in BOTH views), plus horus:react-committed and horus:snapshot-ready. That also removes the polling loop's 3 ms sampling error. If DOM probing is preferred, use `#repository-diff > *` (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:887 sets id="repository-diff" on the diff panel). Raise HORUS_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS above the 4,541 ms snapshot-ready I measured, or the run will still time out on a real repo.
findings.estimatedGainMs: n/a - measurement correctness; without it no startup number can be trusted

findings.title: scripts/check-entry-chunk.mjs now guards a 2.8 KB Vite shim instead of the chunks that actually block mount
findings.mechanism: Since e18053e split main.tsx into a 9-line entry plus a boot chunk, the <script> in out/renderer/index.html points at index-CaNbrFQL.js, which is 2,816 bytes of Vite preload shim. The guard measures that against a 400 KB budget and greps it for "WorkerPool". Meanwhile boot-B2rRKoKF.js is 439,332 bytes (over the budget the guard was written to enforce), and copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js - which DOES contain @pierre/diffs WorkerPoolManager, 20,340 bytes of it - is a static dependency of WorkspaceRoot and therefore on the pre-mount path. The guard passes while the exact thing it was written to prevent has happened.
findings.fix: Rewrite the script to walk the static import graph from the entry chunk plus the `boot` chunk and sum the transitive closure that boot.tsx preloads (WorkspaceRoot + its static deps + whichever viewer branch), then assert that total against a budget (start at the current ~1.9 MB and ratchet down as RB-01..RB-04 land). Keep the WorkerPool assertion but apply it to that closure, not to the shim. Parse the graph out of out/renderer/assets/*.js with the same `from"./X.js"` grep used in this audit, or emit a rollup manifest.
findings.estimatedGainMs: n/a - guardrail; it is what let 1.87 MB creep onto the pre-mount path unnoticed

findings.title: corner-shape: squircle is applied to the universal selector, putting every box on the superellipse paint path
findings.mechanism: The reset rule is `*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; corner-shape: squircle; }`. corner-shape replaces the rounded-rect corner geometry with a superellipse, which is a more expensive clip/paint path than the border-radius fast path, and it is now declared on every element in the document - including the virtualized diff rows and the file-tree rows inside the two shadow roots. It only has a visible effect where border-radius is non-zero, which is a few dozen classes.
findings.fix: Move corner-shape out of the universal rule and onto the elements that actually round: `button, input, select, textarea, dialog, .card, .popover, [data-type="item"], .review-bar, kbd { corner-shape: squircle; }`. Keep box-sizing on `*`. Measure before/after with a paint profile while scrolling the review, since the win is per-frame rather than at boot.
findings.estimatedGainMs: unmeasured at boot (full recalc is 0.2 ms); the plausible win is in scroll paint, not startup

findings.title: SidebarResizer forces a synchronous layout inside the first commit and can cause a second render
findings.mechanism: A useLayoutEffect reads workspace.getBoundingClientRect().width and then writes --sidebar-width on the same element. Reading geometry inside the first layout effect forces Chromium to lay out the freshly committed tree synchronously, inside the 91 ms boot long task. If clampSidebarWidth changes the value it also calls setCommittedWidth, producing a second render plus a localStorage write, and the effect re-runs (committedWidth is in its dep array).
findings.fix: Set --sidebar-width from loadSidebarWidth() as an inline style on the .workspace element at render time (RepositoryWorkspace renders the parent) so no layout read is needed on the first pass, and clamp only in a ResizeObserver / window resize handler. That removes both the forced reflow and the possible second render.

findings.title: Explorer mount work is bounded and virtualized, but the tree reset does a per-directory collapse pass over every folder
findings.mechanism: Nothing renders 20,000 rows - the live DOM has 218 light nodes, 1,291 including shadow roots and 26 tree rows, so @pierre/trees virtualizes correctly and there is no 20k-element React tree. What does scale with path count is the reset path: useFileTree is constructed with `paths: []` and then a layout effect calls model.resetPaths(treePaths) followed, for a git repo, by `for (const directoryPath of [...directoryPaths].reverse()) model.getItem(directoryPath)?.collapse()` - one model lookup and one collapse per directory, which is roughly 3,000-4,000 lookups on a 20k-path repo, on top of getDirectoryPaths itself. Measured supporting costs (bun/JSC): getDirectoryPaths 1.23 ms at 2,621 real paths / 11.06 ms at 20,000; new Set(paths) 0.82 ms at 20,000; createFileSearchIndex 0.46 ms / 3.18 ms.
findings.fix: Pass the real paths to useFileTree at construction (it already takes `paths` and `initialExpansion: 0`) so the model is built collapsed and the explicit collapse loop can be deleted for the initial mount, keeping it only for the incremental "status" mode. Independently, move createFileSearchIndex (useRepositorySearch.ts:42-45) behind requestIdleCallback so the fuzzy index is not built during the boot commit - the palette is warmed on idle anyway (App.tsx:977-982), so the index can be too.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 5-15 ms at mount on a large repo

findings.title: Confirmed clean: StrictMode does not double-invoke in production, React Compiler is active, and fonts do not block text paint
findings.mechanism: Three things that were worth ruling out and are fine. (1) StrictMode: the bundle contains react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.production.js (176,999 of the boot chunk's 439,230 attributed bytes), so the double-invocation is development-only and StrictMode costs one extra component in the tree. (2) React Compiler: babel-plugin-react-compiler with target 19 is wired at electron.vite.config.ts:216-220 and the output contains memo-cache calls - 34 in boot, 27 in WorkspaceRoot, 17 in MultiFileReview - so it runs; the problem is the App bailout in RB-05, not the setup. (3) Fonts: all 14 faces report font-display: swap and only inter-latin-opsz (72,920 B) plus fira-code-latin-wght (36,276 B) load; the two fontsource stylesheets are dynamically imported inside mountApp (boot.tsx:14-15) so they are not in the pre-mount critical path and cannot delay FCP.
findings.fix: No change needed. Do not spend effort here. One small nit: the 133,336-byte inter-latin-ext woff2 is emitted and will be fetched the first time a non-ASCII character renders; if that matters, drop the ext subsets from the fontsource import.

openQuestions: Why did React Compiler bail on App? The build has to be re-run with a logger on babel-plugin-react-compiler to get the bailout reason. My best guesses from reading the source are the four useEffectEvent call sites (App.tsx:214, 758, 830, 894) or the mutable folderPickerOpenRef writes inside useCallback bodies (App.tsx:838-857), but I did not verify by rebuilding.

Was the blocking await in boot.tsx:20-30 added to suppress a visible skeleton flash? If so, does CachedWorkspaceFallback (App.tsx:326-357, capped at 120 rows) look bad enough to justify ~140 ms of blank window - or would a 60 ms delay before showing the fallback get both?

On restore, workspaceView is taken from the cache and App.tsx:907-909 never re-derives it because the cached paint already set appliedSnapshotRef to the same root. Is landing a dirty git repo in single-file view intended, or is that a bug that also happens to break the benchmark (RB-09)?

I could not get a cold-start profile: the app was already running and I deliberately did not restart the user's session. All timings here are warm (V8 code cache populated, asar pages in the OS cache). A first-launch-after-update profile would likely show the 91 ms long task several times larger, which changes the priority ordering of RB-02/RB-03 relative to RB-01.

Does @pierre/diffs actually execute shiki on the main thread, or is the copyFilePath chunk carrying it only for module-graph reasons? Three createHighlighter-family call sites are present in that chunk; whether any run at startup needs a breakpoint or a CPU profile to settle before stubbing them (RB-03).

The 91 ms long task is one opaque block. Splitting it into module-eval vs React-render vs tree-build needs a real CPU profile (Profiler.start + Page.reload over CDP), which requires restarting the app. Worth doing once the user is not mid-session.
